author: KTSM
title: Ysleta ISD faces projected deficit, considers short-term loan - NewsBreak
text:
38 minutes ago
EL PASO, Texas ( KTSM ) — Ysleta Independent School District leaders discussed a projected budget deficit during a Board of Trustees meeting on Wednesday, April 22.
District officials say Ysleta ISD is facing an estimated $16 million shortfall as it prepares for the upcoming school year.
Superintendent Xavier De La Torre said a major factor is a reduction in state funding tied to changes in how school districts are funded.
“We used to get about $10,000 per student. That figure has been reduced to about $8,400 per student,” De La Torre said. “That is why we have lost $11 million on the revenue side of the ledger just in the last two months.”
District leaders also say enrollment is expected to decline by about 1,500 students next year, which could further reduce funding since state aid is based in part on student attendance.
To help close the gap, officials say the district is looking at cost-saving measures, including limiting hiring and relying on natural staff turnover, such as retirements and resignations.
Even with those efforts, district leaders say cash flow remains a challenge. De La Torre said the district may need to rely on short-term loans in the coming years, particularly during months when state funding is not distributed.
“We may as well get used to the idea of short-term loans… because there are certain months where the state doesn’t send you any money,” he said.
According to the district, officials are exploring loan options and expect to bring a proposal before the board next month.
De La Torre said the district could potentially borrow nearly $60 million as it works to manage its finances.
No action was taken during Wednesday’s meeting.
